errors.text: The proposed laser powder-bed-fusion route is fundamentally different from the target's hydride-containing ink extrusion, hydrogen de-binding, and getter-assisted vacuum sintering route.
The hypothesis focuses mainly on W-Mo-Ta-Nb-V or Nb-Mo-Ta-W alloys rather than the target equiatomic Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr Group IV-V alloy family.

It treats interstitial oxygen as an impurity to minimize, whereas the target mechanism deliberately retains approximately 1 wt.% oxygen for interstitial strengthening while controlling phase stability.
High-temperature annealing is substituted for the target water quench from 1500 degrees C, omitting the key suppression of alpha-HCP formation and retention of metastable beta-BCC.
Annealing alone is asserted to reduce interstitial concentration or its effects without evidence of a getter, reactive atmosphere, or other mechanism that would remove oxygen, nitrogen, or carbon.
The oxidation-protection component—silicide coating and self-healing Zr/Hf oxide formation—is entirely absent.
